claim.pdf_says: BLOCK CONTAINS [integer-1 TO] integer-2 {RECORDS / CHARACTERS} -- RECORDS is underlined, CHARACTERS is NOT underlined
claim.why_it_matters: Format 1 FD BLOCK CONTAINS clause: underlining added to CHARACTERS, making an optional (default) word a key word. The same clause on page 532 (Format 2) correctly leaves CHARACTERS un-underlined.

verdict.reasoning: Cropped the 300 dpi render of page 531 (X-15, section 4.2.2 Format 1, the BLOCK CONTAINS clause) at the brace choice: RECORDS carries a clear underline and CHARACTERS has none. Line 24 of page-531.md transcribes it as <u>CHARACTERS</u>. Under the 1985 notation (IV.2.1.4), braces without choice bars mean one stacked option, explicitly specified or implicitly selected. Underlining marks a required key word, so the markdown turns the optional word CHARACTERS into a required key word. That changes the syntax. The claim quotes both sources accurately.
